name: HyperLogLog register cardinality estimator
definition: For 32-bit hashes, m=2^b, 4≤b≤16, M[j]←max(M[j],ρ(w)), E=α_m m²/Σ_j 2^(−M[j]); V=#{j:M[j]=0}. Return m ln(m/V) if E≤2.5m and V>0; otherwise E if E≤2^32/30; otherwise −2^32 ln(1−E/2^32) for E<2^32.
variables: b prefix length; m registers; j prefix integer plus one; w remaining 32−b bits; ρ first one position (all-zero suffix gives 33−b); M registers initialized to zero; V zero register count; E raw estimate; α_m normalization
assumptions: Insertion-only finite stream, stable 32-bit hash, independent uniformly distributed hash words across distinct keys for probabilistic interpretation; repeated keys map identically. Use m=16 to 65536, adequate register width and accurate arithmetic. The original asymptotic error analysis assumes an ideal infinite-bit hash model
limitations: Approximate only; finite hash collisions, small-range bias and saturation affect accuracy. Typical asymptotic relative standard error near 1.04/√m for large m in the ideal model is not a deterministic bound or an unconditional confidence interval. Original 32-bit correction is unsuitable once raw E reaches the hash range; no deletion
failure_conditions: Invalid register dimensions or insufficient rank width
Unstable or unsuitable hashing; incompatible merge configurations
Raw E≥2^32 in large-range correction; report saturation rather than an invalid logarithm
computation: Initialize registers to zero. Split each hash into b prefix bits and suffix, update the addressed register using the maximum of its old value and the suffix rank. Use α_16=0.673, α_32=0.697, α_64=0.709, and α_m=0.7213/(1+1.079/m) for m≥128. Apply the mutually exclusive corrections in the definition; use a stable log1p form for the large-range correction and report unsupported saturation. Merge identically configured states by coordinatewise maximum.

source.citation: Flajolet, Fusy, Gandouet and Meunier (2007), HyperLogLog: the analysis of a near-optimal cardinality estimation algorithm, DMTCS proceedings AH, 137–156, section 1, equation (3), Theorem 1 and section 4, Figure 3. DOI 10.46298/dmtcs.3545. https://dmtcs.episciences.org/en/articles/3545/download

application: General distinct-key cardinality estimation; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Key stream, hash function and register configuration.
mechanism_note: Maxima make repeated identical hashes idempotent and ensure that componentwise maximum of compatible states equals the state obtained from their union. Under independent uniform hashes, each register is empty with probability (1−1/m)^n; the small-range logarithm approximates inversion of the resulting expected empty count. The finite-range logarithm analogously inverts expected hash occupancy approximately. Neither inversion is an exact unbiased estimate. The original practical program uses zero initialization, unlike the analytical presentation; corrections are interpreted as mutually exclusive to avoid overwriting the small-range result. This register-rank mechanism differs from Bloom bit membership.

name: AMS random-sign second frequency moment estimator
definition: For f_x=Σ updates of key x and F₂=Σ_x f_x², Z_j←Z_j+s_j(x)u; X_j=Z_j²; E[X_j]=F₂; Var(X_j)=2(F₂²−Σ_x f_x⁴). Let A_i be independent averages of q=ceil(8/ε²) squares, and Y=median of odd d such averages with d≥8 ln(1/δ). Then Pr(|Y−F₂|>εF₂)≤δ.
variables: f_x net frequency; F₂ second frequency moment; u signed increment; s_j stable random sign map; Z_j accumulator initialized to zero; X_j square; A_i block average; q block size; d odd block count; ε relative tolerance; δ failure probability
assumptions: Finite key universe, fixed finite signed update sequence independent of random maps, exact arithmetic, unbiased four-wise independent signs within each map, mutually independent maps across and within blocks; 0<ε,δ<1. Signed increments follow by linearity from the original unit-insertion formulation
limitations: The mean of squares is unbiased but the median of block averages is not claimed unbiased. Requires bounded arithmetic and storage for sign seeds and accumulators. Fixed-stream probability guarantee does not cover adaptive updates or simultaneous unlimited queries. No recovery of individual frequencies
failure_conditions: Sign family lacks required independence or changes across updates
Integer overflow, invalid block dimensions or adaptive dependence on random maps
computation: Initialize qd accumulators to zero with independent sign maps. For each update add its signed weight to each corresponding accumulator. At query, square each accumulator, average within blocks and take the median. Use the smallest odd d at least max(1,ceil(8 ln(1/δ))). If F₂=0 every accumulator is zero.

source.citation: Alon, Matias and Szegedy (1999), The space complexity of approximating the frequency moments, Journal of Computer and System Sciences 58(1), 137–147, DOI 10.1006/jcss.1997.1545. Author-hosted 2002 manuscript section 2.2, Theorem 2.2, pp. 6–7: https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~nogaa/PDFS/amsz4.pdf ; signed updates and explicit confidence parameters independently derived

application: General estimation of squared frequency norm; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Update stream, random sign families and aggregation dimensions.
mechanism_note: Expand the second and fourth powers of a signed projection. Terms with odd sign multiplicity vanish by four-wise independence; the fourth moment is Σ f_x⁴+6Σ_{x<y} f_x²f_y². Subtract F₂² to obtain the variance. Chebyshev bounds a block failure by 1/4 with q≥8/ε²; Hoeffding bounds the probability of at least half bad independent blocks by exp(−d/8). Unlike Count Sketch per-key signed bucket queries, the square of a scalar projection estimates a global quadratic functional; the nonlinear aggregation and target differ.
